steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Business aims: the general long-term goals of a business - e.g. 'to become the UK's leading online retailer'. Business objectives: specific, measurable targets that help achieve the aim - e.g. 'increase online sales by 15% in 2024'.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Common objectives: survival (especially for new businesses), profit maximisation (maximise difference between revenue and costs), growth (increase size, revenue, market share), customer satisfaction (retain customers, positive reviews), social/ethical objectives (fair trade, reducing carbon footprint).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: SMART objectives: Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound. E.g. 'Increase market share from 10% to 15% within 2 years' - not just 'grow the business'.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Objectives change over time: a new business aims for survival; once established, it shifts to growth and profit maximisation; a mature business may focus on market share or ethical objectives.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain the difference between a business aim and a business objective, giving an example of each. | Write a SMART objective for a new coffee shop that has been trading for 6 months. | Explain why a business's objectives might change as it moves from start-up to an established company.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always write objectives in SMART format - examiners check for all five elements Link objectives to the business's stage of development (new = survival, established = growth) Consider stakeholder conflict when discussing objectives - owners vs employees vs customers
